sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is most likely the bright, hyperintense region in the posterior part of the leg. It extends from around (280, 480) down to (420, 640) and out to the lateral edge near (500, 570).

Several marks fall within this region: 287, 322, 321, 258, 291 and 285. Mark 286, the cyan square, sits at the edge near the vessels, so I excluded it.

The bright region spans roughly x 270–440 and y 470–660, which puts its centre near (350, 570) in the left panel. In the right panel, with an offset of about 686, that corresponds to roughly x 1036, y 570. Mark 321 at (1048, 596) is closest to that centre and lies well inside the bright area.

ANSWER: 321
